name: National Theatre
watch: Ended Shell 2019; named in the May 2026 Bloomberg letter.
why_flagged: Ended Shell 2019; named in the May 2026 Bloomberg letter.
records_note: It posts annual reports with audited accounts for 2019 to 2024, names corporate, trust and individual supporters on site pages, and names its trustees.

name: Dia Art Foundation
watch: Dropped the Sackler name 2019; Schlumberger origin.
why_flagged: Dropped the Sackler name 2019; Schlumberger origin.
records_note: Its Form 990 is public for 2001 to 2025 and a trustees page exists; no annual report turned up, and the site blocked page fetches.

name: Art Institute of Chicago
watch: Crown family and Griffin money; 68 arrests at a 2024 encampment.
why_flagged: Crown family and Griffin money; 68 arrests at a 2024 encampment.
records_note: It posts annual reports from 2003 to 2024 and its Form 990, names supporters undated, and lists its trustees.
other_findings: Epstein link · Thomas Pritzker · documented: Thomas Pritzker is a former chairman of the Art Institute of Chicago. DOJ files show contact with Epstein from 2000 to 2018, planned visits to Epstein's island and advice on staffing it. Pritzker kept in contact with Epstein after the 2008 conviction, and he denies the allegation Virginia Giuffre made against him in a 2016 deposition unsealed in January 2024. Pritzker stepped down as Hyatt executive chairman on 16 February 2026, saying he deeply regrets the association.

name: 4A Centre for Contemporary Asian Art
funding: Creative Australia, Create NSW and the City of Sydney (accommodation grants), plus the Myer Foundation. A patron scheme adds private support.
records_note: Posts annual reports for 2020 to 2025, names donors and sponsors in the 2020 report and lists a ten-member board.

name: Kunstraum Dornbirn
funding: City of Dornbirn, Land Vorarlberg and the federal state, plus members and unnamed sponsors.
records_note: Lists its six-member managing board but shows sponsors as undated logos and posts no annual report or accounts.

name: TAXISPALAIS Kunsthalle Tirol
funding: Tirol's regional kunsthalle; funders not named in readable site text.
records_note: Its parent Tiroler Landesmuseen posts 2024 and 2025 reports, a balance sheet in the Land Tirol holdings report and its supervisory board; funders are logos.

name: National Art Gallery of The Bahamas
funding: Non-profit with a government subvention plus private donors, memberships and admissions.
records_note: It posts audited accounts for 2014 to 2024 and names its board, but no annual reports and no donor list.

name: Fresh Milk Art Platform
funding: Mellon Foundation unrestricted grant of US$350,000 over 2024 to 2026, plus restricted grants of BBD 150,000 in 2024. Runs the FM/CLF fellowship with the Clara Lionel Foundation.
watch: Artist-led platform in Barbados. The 2024 report does not name its restricted-grant donors.
records_note: Posts a 2024 report with financial statements, names funders and its three directors; the accounts are compiled by an accountant, not audited.

name: KX Space / Kryly Khalopa Theatre (Prastora KX, closed 2021)
funding: Independent theatre (founded 2001) running its own venue; art-sale auctions for the BYSOL solidarity fund reported; grant sources not published
watch: Independent venue opened Nov 2014 at Khalturina 2/1 (theatre, gallery, education, community events); director Aksana Haiko. The theatre still produces (2025 'Brest HERstory' audio-walk about women in Brest 1939–45) but its site gives no current base.
records_note: The theatre's site lists productions and one past partner but posts no reports, accounts, funder list or board.

name: Z33
funding: Kunstenhuis of the Province of Limburg.
watch: Partners not listed in readable form.
records_note: Names its twelve board members but shows partners only as undated logos and posts no annual report or accounts.

name: Contour Biennale
funding: Flemish Community and City of Mechelen, with Kunsthal Mechelen as main partner. 2026 international partners include the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation, Mondriaan Fund, Acción Cultural Española and several embassies.
watch: The Gulbenkian Foundation's endowment is Calouste Gulbenkian's oil fortune, which the map counts as Fossil fuels. It is a 2026 partner.
why_flagged: Flemish Community and City of Mechelen, with Kunsthal Mechelen as main partner. 2026 international partners include the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation, Mondriaan Fund, Acción Cultural Española and several embassies.
records_note: The biennale lists partners and individual supporters for 2026 and names its board, but posts no reports and has no accounts filed in the register.

name: Museo Nacional de Arte de Bolivia
funding: Run since 2003 by the Fundación Cultural del Banco Central de Bolivia, a state foundation.
watch: In June 2020 the foundation's new board forced out director Max Hinderer Cruz; CIMAM urged it to withdraw the request.
why_flagged: Run since 2003 by the Fundación Cultural del Banco Central de Bolivia, a state foundation. No outside sponsor is named; donated artworks arrive through the Foreign Ministry.
records_note: The museum's parent foundation posts reports for 2019 to 2025, financial statements for 2018 to 2025 and its council, but no sponsor list.
